answer: An agent marketplace handling wharf deliveries, terrace repairs, and relic appraisals requires every bidding identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days. The contract counts only escrowed funds, so one deposit cannot back several identities at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires 1,000 bonds held simultaneously: names are cheap, but multiplying eligible bidders ties up real capital and costs the attacker a month of liquidity.
